useCaseTemplates.label: Minimal teaching setup
useCaseTemplates.description: Starts with the common course workflow, communication, and core exercise infrastructure.
consequences: Keeps the deployment close to the default teaching and exercise setup.
Leaves optional AI and integration features disabled until explicitly selected.

useCaseTemplates.label: Programming course
useCaseTemplates.description: Emphasizes programming exercises, common exercise infrastructure, and optional online IDE support.
consequences: Keeps programming exercises enabled for code-based assignments.
Leaves Theia as an explicit follow-up decision because it depends on deployment support.
warnings: Programming exercise execution still depends on CI and VCS infrastructure outside this functional model.

useCaseTemplates.label: Exam-focused course
useCaseTemplates.description: Starts with exam and plagiarism support for assessment-heavy courses.
consequences: Enables exam workflows and plagiarism checks.
Keeps AI assistance disabled by default for assessment-sensitive setups.

useCaseTemplates.label: Course with lecture materials
useCaseTemplates.description: Starts with lecture and tutorial group support for material-centered teaching.
consequences: Highlights lecture management and tutorial groups.
Keeps basic exercise support available for assignments around lecture content.

useCaseTemplates.label: AI-enabled course
useCaseTemplates.description: Starts with the standard course setup plus Iris, Athena, Atlas, and Hyperion decisions.
consequences: Enables AI and adaptive learning features that can enrich feedback and tutoring.
Introduces external service and secret-reference requirements for later deployment profile validation.
warnings: AI options are only usable when the selected deployment profile provides the required services.

useCaseTemplates.label: Custom configuration
useCaseTemplates.description: Starts from the feature model defaults and lets the user review every guided decision.
consequences: Uses the current model defaults as the initial selection.
Keeps all guided decisions visible for detailed review.

steps.title: Configuration Goal
steps.description: Choose the starting goal for the configuration.

steps.title: Teaching Content
steps.description: Configure lecture material, tutorial group, course workflow, and communication features.

decisions.question: Which teaching content capabilities should be available?
decisions.description: Select the course-facing content and communication features that teachers normally use.

options.label: Enable lecture materials
options.description: Allow teachers to manage lectures and lecture units.
consequences: Enables lecture management and material workflows.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.lecture.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can publish lecture material, organize lecture units, and connect course content with exercises.
Students get one place to follow lecture-related learning resources.
recommendedWhen: Your course uses slides, recordings, linked resources, or lecture units alongside exercises.
You want course material to stay connected to learning goals and assessments.
thingsToKnow: Lecture material can be enabled without adding AI or external integration features.
This is useful for material-centered courses even when exercises stay simple.

options.label: Enable tutorial groups
options.description: Allow teachers to manage tutorial groups and related course organization.
consequences: Enables tutorial group administration for courses.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.tutorialgroup.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can organize tutorial groups, assign responsible tutors, and track attendance-related course organization.
Students can be managed in smaller teaching groups.
recommendedWhen: Your course uses exercise groups, lab groups, tutorials, or recurring small-group sessions.
Tutors need clear responsibility for a subset of students.
thingsToKnow: This option supports course organization and does not change exercise assessment behavior.
It is most useful for larger courses with multiple tutors or sessions.

options.label: Keep core course workflow
options.description: Keep the mandatory course workflow and communication baseline selected.
consequences: Keeps course creation, access, overview, communication, and notifications available.
warnings: These features are modeled as mandatory baseline capabilities.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can create and manage courses, participants can access course spaces, and communication remains available.
Students receive the baseline course experience needed for the rest of Artemis.
recommendedWhen: Almost every Artemis course needs the standard course workflow and communication baseline.
You want a normal course setup with announcements, access control, and course overview support.
thingsToKnow: These capabilities are treated as baseline functionality in the current model.
Disabling them can make most other course features unusable.

steps.title: Exercise Types
steps.description: Choose the exercise types that should be available in the course setup.

decisions.question: Which exercise types should teachers be able to use?
decisions.description: Exercise choices map directly to functional feature ids and future configuration overlay entries.

options.label: Programming and quiz exercises
options.description: Keep the default programming and quiz exercise baseline enabled.
consequences: Keeps common exercise infrastructure, programming exercises, and quiz exercises available.
warnings: Programming exercises still need CI and VCS capabilities in the deployment profile.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can run programming exercises with individual feedback and quiz exercises with multiple question modes.
Students can practice, submit, and receive feedback through the core exercise workflow.
recommendedWhen: Your course includes code-based assignments, automatically assessed tasks, or quizzes during lectures and exams.
You want a strong default exercise setup for interactive learning.
thingsToKnow: Programming exercises usually require version control and continuous integration to be prepared by administrators.
Quiz exercises work well for practice, live sessions, and exam-style checks.

options.label: Written exercise types
options.description: Enable text, modeling, and file upload exercises.
consequences: Allows teachers to create text, modeling, and file upload assignments.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.text.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
Sets artemis.modeling.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
Sets artemis.file-upload.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can use text, modeling, and file upload exercises for written, diagram-based, or flexible submission tasks.
Students can submit answers beyond source code and quizzes.
recommendedWhen: Your course needs essays, explanations, UML or other modeling tasks, PDFs, images, or other file submissions.
Manual or semi-automatic assessment is part of the teaching concept.
thingsToKnow: These exercise types are especially useful for conceptual understanding and open-ended assignments.
Assessment workflows may rely more on tutors and grading criteria than fully automatic tests.

steps.title: Assessment and Integrity
steps.description: Configure exam, plagiarism, and assessment-adjacent AI support.

decisions.question: Which assessment and integrity capabilities are needed?
decisions.description: These choices affect exam workflows, plagiarism checks, and optional Athena support.

options.label: Enable exams
options.description: Allow exam creation and exam-specific workflows.
consequences: Enables exam workflows for assessment-heavy courses.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.exam.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can create online exams with exam-specific workflows, variants, test runs, and student reviews.
Courses can separate high-stakes assessment from ordinary practice exercises.
recommendedWhen: Your course runs online exams or needs a dedicated exam mode.
You want structured assessment workflows with preparation and review phases.
thingsToKnow: Exam mode is designed for assessment-heavy scenarios and should be planned carefully.
Courses without formal online exams may not need this option.

options.label: Enable plagiarism checks
options.description: Allow plagiarism detection and related integrity workflows.
consequences: Enables plagiarism checks for supported exercise types.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.plagiarism.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can use plagiarism checks for supported exercise types and follow up on identified cases.
Assessment workflows gain additional support for academic integrity.
recommendedWhen: Your course has graded programming, text, or modeling submissions where originality matters.
You need structured support for reviewing potential plagiarism cases.
thingsToKnow: Plagiarism checks support reviewers; they do not replace human judgment.
Students may need clear communication about plagiarism policies.

options.label: Enable Athena
options.description: Enable Athena-backed assessment assistance where supported.
consequences: Enables Athena integration for assessment assistance.
Requires an Athena service endpoint and secret reference in the active deployment profile.
artifactImpacts: Activates the athena Spring profile or equivalent generated overlay entry when artifact generation is implemented.
warnings: Only available when the active deployment profile provides Athena support.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can use Athena-backed assessment assistance for supported exercise types.
Feedback workflows can become more scalable for text, modeling, or programming assessments.
recommendedWhen: Your course has many submissions and wants AI-supported assessment assistance.
You want to explore semi-automatic feedback suggestions while keeping instructors in control.
thingsToKnow: Athena support requires administrator setup before it is useful in a course.
AI-assisted assessment should be introduced with clear review and quality expectations.

steps.title: AI and Integrations
steps.description: Configure adaptive learning, AI tutoring, LTI, and online IDE integration features.

decisions.question: Which AI and adaptive learning features should be enabled?
decisions.description: AI features explain both functional consequences and later deployment profile requirements.

options.label: Enable Atlas
consequences: Enables adaptive learning support.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.atlas.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
enabledOutcome: Instructors and students can work with competencies, learning goals, adaptive learning, and learning analytics.
Students can monitor progress and receive guidance through learning paths.
recommendedWhen: Your course is organized around competencies, learning goals, or adaptive learning activities.
You want stronger insight into student progress and learning outcomes.
thingsToKnow: Atlas is most valuable when competencies and course material are maintained intentionally.
It can be enabled without turning on AI tutoring features.

options.label: Enable Iris AI Tutor
options.description: Enable AI tutoring support through Iris.
consequences: Enables AI tutoring functionality.
Requires Pyris service and a configured secret reference.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.iris.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
Adds Pyris URL and secret-reference mappings when a deployment profile provides them.
warnings: Only available when the active deployment profile provides AI tutoring support.
enabledOutcome: Students and instructors can receive AI tutoring support for questions, learning progress, and next-step guidance.
The course can offer more immediate support outside direct instructor or tutor availability.
recommendedWhen: Your course wants AI-assisted help for students or instructors.
You expect many recurring questions around exercises, lectures, or learning progress.
thingsToKnow: Iris requires administrator setup before users can benefit from it.
AI tutoring should complement, not replace, course staff and official feedback.

options.label: Enable Hyperion
options.description: Enable Hyperion functionality for future AI-supported workflows.
consequences: Enables Hyperion support.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.hyperion.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
warnings: Only available when the active deployment profile provides Hyperion support.
enabledOutcome: Instructors can use AI-supported workflows for creating and improving exercises.
Course teams can get assistance with consistency and quality checks during exercise preparation.
recommendedWhen: Your course team wants AI assistance while authoring exercises.
Exercise quality, consistency, or drafting effort is a recurring concern.
thingsToKnow: Hyperion requires administrator setup for AI services.
Generated or suggested content should still be reviewed by instructors.

decisions.question: Which platform integrations should be enabled?
decisions.description: Integration choices connect Artemis to external learning tools or IDE services.

options.label: Enable LTI
consequences: Allows Artemis to integrate with LTI-capable learning platforms.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.lti.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
warnings: LTI requires external platform registration data before deployment.
enabledOutcome: Artemis can be integrated with external learning platforms that support LTI.
Students and instructors can access Artemis activities from another learning management system.
recommendedWhen: Your institution uses another LMS as the main course entry point.
You want Artemis to fit into an existing platform ecosystem.
thingsToKnow: LTI setup requires administrator coordination with the external learning platform.
Courses that use Artemis directly may not need this integration.

options.label: Enable Theia
options.description: Enable online IDE support through Theia.
consequences: Enables online IDE support for programming workflows.
artifactImpacts: Sets artemis.theia.enabled = true in the generated external configuration overlay.
warnings: Only available when online IDE infrastructure is provided by the deployment profile.
enabledOutcome: Students can work on programming exercises in an online IDE without local setup.
Instructors can offer a smoother start for programming tasks.
recommendedWhen: Your course includes programming exercises and wants to reduce local setup friction.
Students use diverse devices or may not have a prepared development environment.
thingsToKnow: Online IDE support requires administrator-provided infrastructure.
Students may still choose a local IDE when the course allows it.

steps.title: Review and Consequences
steps.description: Summarize selected features, unavailable capabilities, warnings, and consequences.

steps.title: Artifact Generation
steps.description: Prepare the later artifact-generation handoff from a validated configuration.
